rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 602.1, best so far): oval finishes 19 of 20 (progress 0.99), s-bend finishes 9 of 20 (progress 0.95), and slalom finishes 1 of 20 (progress 0.53, 0.95 line-loss events per run, max_error 0.0615). steering_oscillation is 0.27 to 0.40, well below the 0.5 warning level, so damping is not the limit. The failures are off-track drift on bends. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at body_width 0.18 that is 0.0575, so the limit stays at 0.06 and body width cannot help. Changing the spread from +/-0.035 to +/-0.04 m moved slalom progress from 0.42 to 0.53 and line losses from 1.05 to 0.95, a small gain, so edge coverage is not the main limit. The more likely cause is lag: the sensors sit only 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the robot only sees a bend after its wheels are already on it. Changes: (1) Move all five sensors forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m, keeping the same x spread (-0.04 to +0.04 m) and spacing. This gives a longer preview of the tape, adding phase lead so the correction starts earlier on alternating bends. (2) All other values are kept at iteration 5 (kp 5.0, kd 1.4, ki 0.01, base_speed 1.2, sensor_size 0.016, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, sensor weights, line_loss last_direction) so the effect of the sensor position can be read cleanly. Expected result: slalom max_error and line-loss events fall, slalom progress rises above 0.7, and s-bend completion improves. Oval should hold near 0.95 completion. Hypotheses: (a) if the sensor move makes steering_oscillation rise above about 0.5, the extra lead is overcorrecting and kd should be kept or kp reduced to about 4.6. (b) If slalom progress is unchanged, lag is not the limit and the next step is more steering authority (kp about 5.5 with kd 1.5) or a narrower wheel_track of about 0.10 m to raise turn rate per unit turn. (c) If s-bend finishes stay under 10 of 20 while oval holds, base_speed should drop to about 1.15 again. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so the sensor-lead effect can be separated from gain effects.
